resources.string: When blood calcium falls, parathyroid chief cells release parathyroid hormone (PTH) to help regulate it. After secretion, the hormone can bind to receptors on target cells and start a response. This analogy shows only binding of an imaginary signal, not how strongly a cell responds. Both sliders use made-up, unitless numbers, not personal records or real receptor affinity. This model does not predict PTH or blood calcium levels.
Occupied percent = 100 × s ÷ (s + k). When s equals k, half the sites are occupied. At fixed k, as s rises, occupancy approaches 100 percent in smaller and smaller steps.
